operations.content: Actual shutdown sequence: main() creates Application on stack, calls init()/run(), then returns. Stack unwinding triggers ~Application() (line 186) which calls shutdown() (line 174). shutdown() explicitly calls CustomHeapManager destructor (line 177), sets g_custom_heap=nullptr (line 178), then frees heap_memory (line 179). This happens ONCE, not twice.

Correct root cause: Static objects from libstdc++ (in release version) get allocated using custom heap after g_custom_heap is set at line 149. When program exits, heap_memory is freed at line 179, but static destructors run AFTER main() returns, trying to access/free memory from the already-freed custom heap, causing SIGSEGV in release mode.

Step 10: Corrected root cause understanding. No double-destruction bug exists. Real issue: static libstdc++ objects allocated from custom heap, destroyed after heap freed. Ready to implement fix: trigger stdlib initialization in user_init() (before line 149) to ensure static objects use regular malloc instead of custom heap.

When the program exits, heap_memory is freed at line 179, but static destructors run AFTER main() returns, trying to access/free memory from the already-freed custom heap.

The shutdown sequence happens once, not twice (confirmed in [csHvGg5X]).

The fix is ready to implement: Trigger stdlib initialization in user_init() (which is called at line 146, before g_custom_heap setup at line 149). This ensures static objects use regular malloc instead of the custom heap.
